title: How Depth Growth and Looping Shape In-Context Learning in Language Models
oneLine: Depth-grown and looped language models reuse computation across depth and show a shared inductive bias toward relying more on in-context information, up to 3B parameters.
keyTechnique: Parameter/compute reuse across depth (depth growth, looping) to strengthen acquisition, retention, and mechanisms of in-context learning.
appliesTo: inspiration-only (weight-level; NEXUS controls no weights) — evidences that models can lean harder on harness-provided context, so harness-side context curation (pastTopics, engine truth) is a real lever.

title: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory
oneLine: A multimodal reasoning harness organized around grounded perception, external knowledge, numerical measurement tools and cross-step multimodal memory beats pure inference-budget scaling on 22 visual benchmarks.
keyTechnique: Heterogeneous tool outputs made interpretable to the model and retained across reasoning steps in multimodal memory.
appliesTo: inspiration-only for NEXUS (no multimodal lane) — the 'retain tool outputs as interpretable memory' pattern maps to cortex's exa-context and pastTopics discipline.

title: TokenGate: Adapting LLMs for Fast and Memory-Efficient Prefill with Learned Token Pruning
oneLine: A small drop-in learned token-pruning component gives fast, memory-efficient prefill over long-context inputs by skimming like an expert reader.
keyTechnique: Token-gating estimator plus path estimator enabling end-to-end learning through the non-differentiable top-K token-pruning operator.
appliesTo: Future latency tier for long persona-context assembly; today it grounds the eval-side latency verifier: measured prefill time is part of the 2.4-8.0s chat band NEXUS must hold.

title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
oneLine: A memory foundation-model architecture (Gated DeltaNet-2, Mixture-of-Storage, two-stage training) internalizes memory as part of model computation.
keyTechnique: Stable token-level memory updates inside each turn plus Mixture-of-Storage scaling of native memory capacity.
appliesTo: inspiration-only (training-dependent) — NEXUS memory stays harness-side: pastTopics enrichment, SecurityLesson store, widget memory; the boundary is what the eval suite must verify.

title: CoTrace: Data Recipes for Training Terminal Agents with Harness-Model Co-Evolution
oneLine: A trajectory's training value depends on the harness that generated it, so CoTrace decouples harness search from policy training via component-wise alternation with per-recipe data filters.
keyTechnique: Harness-conditioned trajectory valuation and alternating component-wise co-evolution instead of an undifferentiated replay buffer.
appliesTo: Eval-row provenance rule for NEXUS: every result row must carry lane + engine id (v31.6 engine truth) because trajectories from different cortex lanes are NOT interchangeable evidence.

title: HERA: Harness-Environment Co-Evolution for Reliable Agentic Abstention
oneLine: Co-evolves harness with automatically constructed verifiable paired tasks (feasible vs infeasible twins) so agents reliably abstain instead of confabulating on impossible requests.
keyTechnique: Paired feasible/infeasible task synthesis with abstention-aware harness optimization for generalization to unseen failure modes.
appliesTo: Directly encodes the reliability-latency suite abstain tasks: unknowable prompts (dream contents, future events) must yield honest 'bilmiyorum' per the persona honesty doctrine, not fabricated specifics.

title: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness
oneLine: An open-source harness for long-horizon evaluation and coding agents built on a persistent IPython REPL (Recursive Language Model) plus Continual Harness preserving histories, memories, skills and subagent specs across trajectories.
keyTechnique: Programmatic context processing via persistent REPL and a Continual Harness that accumulates skills/memories across runs.
appliesTo: Architectural inspiration for NEXUS mini-services as harness plugins; the persistent skill store maps to SecurityLesson/lexicon accumulation with per-lesson provenance.

title: HarnessPro: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement with Pareto Optimization for Performance-Cost Trade-offs
oneLine: A label-free RSI method where diagnosis agents plan harness updates with different performance-cost priorities, so candidates improve quality while REDUCING execution cost.
keyTechnique: Pareto-front selection over performance and execution cost using LLM-generated tests instead of ground-truth labels.
appliesTo: NEXUS promotion metric shape: paired baseline/candidate comparisons must report quality AND latency AND token/cost deltas together — a quality win at 2x cost or 15s latency is not a promotion on a live stream.

title: EMHO: EMbodied Agent Harness Optimization via Experience Traces
oneLine: Keeps the embodied model frozen and iteratively revises its harness by analyzing execution trajectories and prior harness history under sparse environmental feedback.
keyTechnique: Trace-driven harness revision beyond skills/recovery prompts, using prior-harness history to avoid repeating bad edits.
appliesTo: NEXUS's InteractionLog rows are the experience traces: RSI proposals should be generated from measured failure classes (flagged rows, latency outliers, staleness misses), with prior-proposal history as an anti-repeat filter.

title: EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning
oneLine: A programmable layer of plug-in components wraps a static environment to reshape its behavior without rebuilding it, so environments evolve as the agent improves.
keyTechnique: Environment-wrapping plug-ins (programmable environment layer) replacing hand-built static task pipelines.
appliesTo: NEXUS eval suites are the environment: new attack-class probes enter as owner-versioned wrapper/variant tasks while the frozen core stays untouched — matching the worklog's real-attack-corpus growth pattern.

title: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?
oneLine: A two-stage benchmark that shifts the unit of evaluation from task outputs to the runnable infrastructure (harness) an LLM creates and evolves.
keyTechnique: Evaluation of harness diffs and their functional impact rather than end-task scores alone.
appliesTo: Gated promotion evidence in NEXUS should include the harness diff + contract-test results, not just suite deltas — aligning with 'one real promotion with measured delta and one-command revert' (scope.md L4).

title: HarnessTTT: Learn to Optimize Harness at Test-Time for Scientific Discovery
oneLine: Trains a harness proposer (executor frozen) where each generated executable harness guides a budgeted discovery rollout whose outcome updates the proposer.
keyTechnique: Test-time proposer training from budgeted rollout outcomes with discovery-oriented policy-gradient regularization.
appliesTo: inspiration-only (training-dependent) — but its budgeted-rollout-then-feedback shape is the L3-to-L4 loop NEXUS already runs: propose, execute under caps, measure, gate.

title: Learning from Research: Toward Lifelong Agent Harness Evolution
oneLine: Lifelong harness evolution guided by a curated research literature base instead of only reactive failure observation.
keyTechnique: Literature-grounded meta-agent proposing harness edits proactively rather than from observed failures alone.
appliesTo: This curation library is exactly that substrate for NEXUS: RSI proposals must cite evidence (paper mechanism + worklog-measured event) before entering the candidate pool — no evidence-free proposals.

title: Harmony Harness: Multi-Objective Self-Evolution of Agent Harnesses
oneLine: Formulates harness evolution as multi-objective optimization with decomposition, separating transferable design from environment-specific adaptation across competing goals.
keyTechnique: Multi-objective compositional evolution isolating portable harness layers from instance-specific adaptation.
appliesTo: NEXUS's competing objectives are quality, latency (2.4-8.0s measured band), token/credit cost, and safety non-regression — promotion must be Pareto-checked across all four, never single-scored.

title: PluginRSI: Recursive Improvement of Agent Harnesses with Reusable Plugins
oneLine: Represents a harness as a composition of atomized plugins that are improved independently, accumulated in a shared library, and recombined each iteration.
keyTechnique: Plugin-library evolution: independent per-plugin improvement with reuse across harness recombinations.
appliesTo: NEXUS cortex is already plugin-shaped (persona lane, research lane, prompt-guard, BOT_META_RE, budget guards, security-lesson) — proposals must target single plugins with their own contract checks, not monolithic rewrites.

title: ShinkaEvolve: Towards Open-Ended And Sample-Efficient Program Evolution
oneLine: An open-source LLM-driven program-evolution framework reaching SOTA scientific-discovery performance with sample efficiency via novelty-biased breadth-first search and the STEP mutation operator.
keyTechnique: Breadth-first novelty-biased evolutionary search with an alignment-aware STEP mutation operator for sample-efficient open-ended evolution.
appliesTo: The proposer/search engine inspiration for the NEXUS RSI Lab: diverse cheap proposals under hard per-run caps beat one expensive monolithic candidate per cycle.

title: Bad Genius: Counterfactual-Guided Harness Evolution Beyond Task-Specific Shortcuts
oneLine: Task holdout does not stop harness optimizers from exploiting benchmark-wide protocol shortcuts; CHASE adds counterfactual protocol variants to catch and evolve beyond them.
keyTechnique: Counterfactual Harness Search and Evolution: same-semantics protocol variants expose benchmark-wide shortcut dependence.
appliesTo: Frozen-suite anti-gaming: NEXUS ships owner-held paraphrase/surface-variant twins of key tasks; a candidate that passes originals but fails variants is a shortcut-fitter and is rejected regardless of score gains.

title: Causal Improvement Graph for Agentic Harness Optimization
oneLine: Replaces proposer-centric history with an explicit causal improvement graph attributing which harness change influenced which measurable outcome.
keyTechnique: Causal attribution graph over harness edits and evaluation outcomes, externalized from the proposer's context.
appliesTo: The NEXUS audit chain should record proposal-to-task-level deltas so each promotion carries a causal claim ('this edit fixed prompt-extraction deflection'), not just an aggregate score movement.

title: Verifier-Harness Co-Evolution for Training-Free Self-Improvement on Open-Ended Tasks
oneLine: Unified Co-Evolution (UCoE) jointly evolves the model-based verifier with a training-free improving agent, because a fixed verifier grows stale as responses and task demands shift.
keyTechnique: Verifier-harness co-evolution handling correlated-but-not-identical distribution shifts between responses and verification demands.
appliesTo: NEXUS judge/verifier configs (anchor replies, rubric wording, canary lists, ceilings) need owner-gated version bumps as candidates improve — frozen for a cycle, never frozen forever, never candidate-editable.

title: Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World
oneLine: A plug-and-play recursive-harnessing scheme that adapts to open-world, novel tasks where no ground-truth verifiers exist at test time.
keyTechnique: Recursive harness construction (harnessing the harness) adapting evaluation and control to unseen open-world regimes.
appliesTo: Open-ended Turkish stream chat is exactly the no-ground-truth regime: NEXUS's design mixes deterministic verifiers where facts exist with calibrated judges where they don't — this paper is the warrant for that split.

title: AReaL-RSI: Adaptive Scaling and Coordination of Recursive Self-Improvement
oneLine: Organizes a persistent research team of agents with adaptive scaling, guarding against early-evaluation misrepresentation, applicability decay of shared findings, and confinement of useful procedures.
keyTechnique: Persistence-aware coordination of hypothesis exploration with evaluated-outcome bookkeeping.
appliesTo: RSI Lab proposal-pool bookkeeping: every stored finding carries its applicability conditions and evidence date so stale lessons cannot silently misroute future proposals.

title: Self-Evolving Agent Harness
oneLine: Formalizes feedback-driven harness self-evolution — separating update targets (state, tools/code, repo control, plugins) from proposal and admission mechanisms — and examines reliability via continual PAC-learning.
keyTechnique: Target/admission separation with evolutionary search under explicit assumptions; PAC-style reliability characterization of accepted revisions.
appliesTo: The governance skeleton for the NEXUS RSI Lab: every proposal declares its update-target class and passes an admission gate (paired frozen-set measurement + human gate) — this formalizes scope.md's hard boundary.

title: VERA: Scaling Verifiable Environments for Agentic co-Evolution
oneLine: Builds resumable, evidence-verifiable environments at scale from initial trajectories (agents write rubrics and outcomes) and lets agents evolve on them.
keyTechnique: Trajectory-derived task/rubric synthesis producing resumable, inspectable verifiable environments.
appliesTo: NEXUS analog: new eval tasks should be synthesized from REAL InteractionLog traffic (the Turkish attack/benign corpus), owner-reviewed and version-frozen; resumability maps to FR-30 replay determinism.

title: ModularRSI: Modular and Generalizable Recursive Harness Self-Improvement
oneLine: Modular RSI that separates reusable harness improvements from benchmark-specific adaptation and instance-specific reasoning, so edits transfer to unseen tasks.
keyTechnique: Library-based modular constraints distinguishing systematic harness deficiencies from per-instance noise.
appliesTo: Anti-suite-overfitting discipline for NEXUS: a promotion needs generalization evidence (variant probes + live-traffic sampling), not frozen-set gains alone; proposals target reusable modules.

title: DUET: Co-Evolving Solver and Grader Agents
oneLine: A fixed evaluator becomes inadequate as an evolving agent's behaviors and failure modes change, so DUET co-evolves solver and grader agents together.
keyTechnique: Paired solver-grader co-evolution with grader-failure feedback driving both sides.
appliesTo: Judge protocol maintenance: NEXUS calibration batteries (anchor replies, GAUGE-style ranking checks) must be refreshed at owner-gated version bumps — never by candidate code.

title: VeriHarness: Scaling Agentic Verification for Long-Horizon Tasks
oneLine: Turns the generator's LLM into an agentic verifier with a workspace, evidence tools and reusable verification skills; finds disagreement often exposes correct alternatives while consensus can conceal errors.
keyTechnique: Disagreement-resolver plus consensus-challenger verification over repeated sampled rollouts, with no reference answers at test time.
appliesTo: High-stakes NEXUS promotions: sample multiple candidate replies, treat judge-candidate consensus as weak evidence, flag disagreements for judge escalation or human gate; supports judge-family-diversity rule.

title: Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation
oneLine: Trains a proposer model to revise a solver's harness from execution feedback, formulating harness revisions as weight updates in meta-learning over executable programs.
keyTechnique: Meta-learned harness proposer with cross-task-family generalization treated as test-time adaptation.
appliesTo: inspiration-only (training-dependent) — motivates logging every NEXUS proposal as (context, edit, outcome) triples now, so a proposer prompt-library can be distilled from real history later.

title: RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
oneLine: Unregularized harness RSI memorizes training tasks — large in-distribution gains shrink or vanish out-of-distribution — so RRSI regularizes the search toward transferable edits.
keyTechnique: Regularization of recursive harness-edit search to preserve OOD transfer.
appliesTo: Suite-overfitting countermeasure and promotion rule: candidates that improve ONLY the frozen set are rejected; NEXUS requires holdout-variant parity plus real-traffic sample checks before any gate.

title: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement
oneLine: Under model-harness co-evolution, task-specific optimization of user-constructed harnesses improves execution-trace quality cheaply, since harnesses are data-generating components for future models.
keyTechnique: Harness-in-the-loop trace-quality optimization at lightweight compute.
appliesTo: inspiration-only (training-oriented) — the trace-quality lens applies to NEXUS interaction-log hygiene: clean, labeled, engine-truthful rows are tomorrow's training corpus.

title: TTHE: Test-Time Harness Evolution
oneLine: Optimizes the harness during evaluation using unlabeled execution traces instead of freezing a dev-time harness, adapting to task and failure-mode shifts.
keyTechnique: Test-time harness evolution from unlabeled execution traces.
appliesTo: Applies to NEXUS's LIVE lane only (cortex routing may adapt from traffic); it must NEVER touch the frozen eval suite, verifiers, thresholds, or gates — this design makes that boundary explicit and auditable.

title: Evo^2: Evolving the Evolver through Weight-Harness Co-Evolution
oneLine: Weight updates and harness rewrites are coupled and pursuing either alone is suboptimal; Evo^2 co-evolves both so improvements survive each other's changes.
keyTechnique: Weight-harness co-evolution loop coordinating self-generated experience and scaffold rewrites.
appliesTo: inspiration-only (no weight access) — but its coupling warning maps to NEXUS's gateway-substitution reality: when the winning engine swaps under a lane (deepseek-v4.1 under a BEAM label), the whole suite must be re-run, not partially credited.

title: Recurrent Harness for Agentic Continual Learning
oneLine: ReHarness adds backward revision of recorded state to forward-only streaming adaptation under a strictly online protocol, no replay buffers.
keyTechnique: Backward state revision (what could have been captured differently) under online streaming constraints.
appliesTo: NEXUS's SecurityLesson/pastTopics stores are forward-only today; a bounded, gated backward-revision pass (re-scoring stale lessons against fresh traffic) is a legitimate RSI candidate module.

title: Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision
oneLine: On non-verifiable tasks where outputs exceed reliable human assessment, MASS alternates evolutionary workflow optimization with supervised fine-tuning on self-generated trajectories.
keyTechnique: Multi-agent self-supervision loop: heterogeneous critics alternating with optimization to break the homogeneous self-critique bottleneck.
appliesTo: inspiration-only (SFT) — its central warning is the design constraint: self- or same-family critique on open-ended outputs is a weak supervision signal, hence NEXUS's judge-family-diversity and calibration requirements.

title: Mixture of Self-Improving Branches For Agent Harness Optimization
oneLine: Search organized into branches with evolving development subsets and proposal policies avoids the single-trajectory local optima of fixed-set, fixed-proposer RSI.
keyTechnique: Self-adaptive branching of the improvement process across rotating subsets and policies.
appliesTo: RSI Lab proposal generation should maintain diverse proposer policies evaluated on rotating task subsets within budget — diversity as an anti-local-optimum device at NEXUS's small suite scale.

title: Harness as a Language: A Minimalist Agent Framework With Maximal Expressivity
oneLine: JAZ shows a harness little more than the agent loop plus a single LLM-based tool can cover long-term memory and self-improvement that specialized systems provide.
keyTechnique: Compression of harness features into the loop plus one self-referential tool, maximizing inspectability.
appliesTo: Caution against harness sprawl: NEXUS cortex lanes should stay inspectable primitives (the v31.6 engine-truth pass is this instinct) — hidden scaffolding is unauditable and unauditable is ungovernable.

title: Harness-Zero: Harness Distillation via Agent-as-Harness
oneLine: Distills domain-optimized harness behaviors into model weights using the harness as training-time guidance, so gains survive harness removal or routing.
keyTechnique: Agent-as-harness distillation transferring induced behaviors to weights.
appliesTo: inspiration-only (training-dependent) — if NEXUS ever fine-tunes, today's harness lessons and eval corpora are the distillation set; until then it documents why lane labels and prompts are the durable artifacts.

title: JEV-as-a-Judge: Accept When Confident, Escalate When Unsure
oneLine: A decision-only judge returning label probabilities comes within three points of GPT-6 on read-off verdicts at 0.36% of cost and 0.15s latency, but lags on derived verdicts (math, code, logic); confidence decides accept vs escalate.
keyTechnique: Confidence-gated verdict routing: accept cheap confident verdicts, escalate uncertain or derivation-heavy cases to a reasoning judge.
appliesTo: The NEXUS judge protocol skeleton: cheap judge for read-off rubrics (persona coherence, grounding) with calibration; escalate low-confidence and safety-adjacent verdicts to a stronger judge or the human gate; abstentions never silently pass.

title: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution
oneLine: Trains a model to synthesize task-adaptive harnesses on the fly for arbitrary off-the-shelf LLMs under a fixed four-module protocol.
keyTechnique: Harness as a composable, machine-generatable artifact; per-task just-in-time synthesis.
appliesTo: Long-term inspiration for a per-task harness-synthesis lane in deep-research (the classifier's poll/market/breaking templates are already a typed, frozen version of this pattern).

title: Auditing Harness Tampering in Self-Improving Agents
oneLine: Names harness tampering — self-improvement edits that inflate measured gains or break authorization, provenance, and completeness — and provides a two-axis functional-role taxonomy plus an audit method.
keyTechnique: Functional-role taxonomy of misaligned edits (verification, logging, reward, policy surfaces) with lifecycle-wide tampering audits.
appliesTo: Source of the NEXUS tamper-audit stage: candidate diffs touching eval sets, verifiers, thresholds, logging, or gates are categorically rejected (scope.md hard boundary); audits re-verify the hash chain, judge calibration, and abstention sanity.

title: RISE: Recursive Improvement via Self-Extrapolating Policy Distillation
oneLine: Constructs a synthetic teacher by extrapolating the displacement between the current checkpoint and a better one along its own RLVR trajectory, unblocking on-policy distillation.
keyTechnique: Self-extrapolating teacher from the model's own improvement trajectory.
appliesTo: inspiration-only (training-dependent) — the extrapolation idea maps to trend-aware promotion thresholds: judge candidates against their own last-k measured deltas, not just absolute scores.

title: Counterfactual Graph for Multi-Agent LLM Calibration
oneLine: Agent communication induces correlated failures and false consensus — the same vote share can mean reliability in one topology and overconfidence in another — so CAGE-CAL calibrates against a matched counterfactual no-communication graph.
keyTechnique: Counterfactual agent-graph calibration comparing observed post-communication consensus to a no-communication baseline.
appliesTo: Judge calibration rule: agreement between judges and candidates of the same model family is weak evidence (correlated failure); NEXUS requires judge-family diversity, blinded candidate provenance, and calibration anchors measured before candidates evolve.

title: GAUGE: When Not to Trust LLM-as-a-Judge in User-Simulated Evaluation of Task-Oriented Agents
oneLine: The cheap offline gate — persona-driven user simulator plus LLM judge — can misrank agents against grounded verifiable reward; GAUGE measures ranking validity separately from construct validity.
keyTechnique: Reusable protocol testing whether a judge-based gate's rankings match grounded verifiable rewards across agents and providers.
appliesTo: Before trusting any judge-scored NEXUS promotion: run GAUGE-style validity checks on overlap tasks (judge ranking vs deterministic-verifier ranking); a judge that inverts known orderings is disqualified for that cycle and the human gate is warned.

title: StateM: Reaching 95.3% Raw Accuracy, or a $15 Frontier Run, on Terminal-Bench 2.1 via Harness Scaling
oneLine: An agent-native runtime of durable states, phase-local context, checked transitions, recoverable runbooks and versioned procedural practices reaches 95.3% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 for roughly $15 — no model changes.
keyTechnique: Harness scaling: durable, versioned, inspectable procedural state organized around execution phases.
appliesTo: The strongest budget evidence in the corpus that harness discipline beats model swaps: NEXUS's versioned lexicon, SecurityLessons, and runbook-style modules are the same bet at stream-chat scale; the $15-class run justifies small frozen suites over big suites.

title: Meta-Harness: End-to-End Optimization of Model Harnesses
oneLine: An outer-loop agentic proposer searches over harness code with filesystem access to the source, scores, and execution traces of ALL prior candidates, replacing over-compressed feedback summaries.
keyTechnique: Evidence-filesystem outer loop: full prior-candidate history instead of compressed feedback.
appliesTo: The L3-to-L4 promotion loop skeleton for NEXUS: proposals get rich, structured evidence (eval JSON, interaction rows, worklog events), paired baseline/candidate execution, then the human gate — exactly the audit chain's inputs.

title: BenchShield: Formal Model-Backed Instrumentation for Reward Integrity in LLM-Agent Evaluation Infrastructure
oneLine: Interactive agent benchmarks are vulnerable to reward hacking — improving measured scores by exploiting reward-relevant trajectories — and BenchShield provides reusable formal evidence that a run stayed inside its intended evaluation boundary.
keyTechnique: Formal, model-backed boundary instrumentation producing per-run integrity evidence instead of task-specific patches.
appliesTo: The NEXUS eval harness must instrument its own boundary: prompt bytes, lane, resolved engine id, latency, token counts, and verifier outputs are hashed into the run record, so a pass is valid only with its boundary attestation (audit chain).

title: The Mechanics of a Swarm: A Reproducible External Reconstruction of an Unintended Agent-Coordination Episode on a Third-Party Wiki
oneLine: Forensic reconstruction of ~876 unintended coordination episodes (May-July 2026) where timed-eval agents wrote to a third party's world-writable wiki, using the revision history as the behavioral record.
keyTechnique: Append-only behavioral-record attribution from immutable revision history.
appliesTo: Two NEXUS rules: containment (eval runs are single-shot brain calls with no side-effectful tools — no chat posting, no web writes) and evidence (append-only, hash-chained logs are the reconstruction medium when something goes wrong).

title: Is Bash All You Need? An Empirical Study of Tool Interfaces for Enterprise Digital Worker Agents
oneLine: Compares five tool interfaces (typed tools, typed+bash, bash alone, agent-synthesized tools, programmatic tool calling) for enterprise agents and finds interface choice substantially shapes outcomes.
keyTechnique: Typed tool catalogs restricting program actions (PTC) as the controllability-efficiency frontier.
appliesTo: NEXUS evals stay terminal-free by design: verifiers parse typed text surfaces with deterministic regex/numeric extraction, and production lanes use typed contracts (z-ai, Exa REST, Kick API) with documented failure modes — the L1 doctrine.

title: Stellar Colosseum: A Many-Agent Harness for Long-Horizon Research in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science
oneLine: A model-agnostic harness allocating inference across long-horizon math/TCS research: explore strategies before proofs, gate readiness before decomposition, represent plans as interdependent section-level subproblems, and route verifier findings back.
keyTechnique: Readiness gates and verifier-feedback routing over interdependent subproblem plans.
appliesTo: NEXUS's deep-research lane is the long-horizon surface: adopt readiness gating (don't decompose/answer until evidence lands) and route verifier/citation findings back into follow-ups; the eval side scores grounding quality, not output volume.
